7607-zicci-a-tale-volume-02.title: Zicci A Tale Volume 02
7607-zicci-a-tale-volume-02.creator: Unknown
7607-zicci-a-tale-volume-02.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Zicci paused, and drew Glyndon aside. "Young man," said he, gravely, "it is necessary that we should again meet to-night. It is necessary that you should, ere the first hour of morning, decide on your fate. There are times in life when from the imagination, and not the reason, should wisdom come,--this for you is one of them.

arxiv-2011-09740.title: Wall shear stress distribution in a compliant airway tree
arxiv-2011-09740.creator: Jonathan Stéphano, Benjamin Mauroy
arxiv-2011-09740.description: Abstract The airflow in the bronchi applies a shear stress on the bronchial mucus, which can move the mucus. The air–mucus interaction plays an important role in cough and in chest physiotherapy (CP). The conditions under which it induces a displacement of the mucus are still unclear.

arxiv-2203-15272.title: Sparse Image based Navigation Architecture to Mitigate the need of precise Localization in Mobile Robots
arxiv-2203-15272.creator: Pranay Mathur, Rajesh Kumar, Sarthak Upadhayay
arxiv-2203-15272.description: Abstract Traditional simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) methods focus on improvement in the robot’s localization under environment and sensor uncertainty. This paper, however, focuses on mitigating the need for exact localization of a mobile robot to pursue autonomous navigation using a sparse set of images.

arxiv-2208-13794.title: Seeking dark matter with γ \gamma -ray attenuation
arxiv-2208-13794.creator: José Luis Bernal, Andrea Caputo, Gabriela Sato-Polito, Jordan Mirocha, Marc Kamionkowski
arxiv-2208-13794.description: Abstract The flux of high-energy astrophysical γ \gamma rays is attenuated by the production of electron-positron pairs from scattering off of extragalactic background light (EBL). We use the most up-to-date information on galaxy populations to compute their contributions to the pair-production optical depth.

arxiv-2209-06753.title: Modelling polarity-driven laminar patterns in bilayer tissues with mixed signalling mechanisms
arxiv-2209-06753.creator: Joshua W. Moore 1, Trevor C. Dale 2, Thomas E. Woolley 1
arxiv-2209-06753.description: Abstract . Recent advances in high-resolution experimental methods have highlighted the significance of cell signal pathway crosstalk and localised signalling activity in the development and disease of numerous biological systems. The investigation of multiple signal pathways often introduces different methods of cell-cell communication, i.e. contact-based or diffusive signalling, which generates both a spatial and temporal dependence on cell behaviours.

arxiv-2211-13536.title: Proprioceptive Sensing of Soft Tentacles with Model Based Reconstruction for Controller Optimization
arxiv-2211-13536.creator: Andrea Vicari*, Nana Obayashi*, Francesco Stella, Gaetan Raynaud, Karen Mulleners, Cosimo Della Santina, Josie Hughes
arxiv-2211-13536.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Andrea Vicari*, Nana Obayashi*, Francesco Stella, Gaetan Raynaud, Karen Mulleners, Cosimo Della Santina, Josie Hughes. The success of soft robots in displaying emergent behaviors is tightly linked to the compliant interaction with the environment. However, to exploit such phenomena, proprioceptive sensing methods which do not hinder their softness are needed.

arxiv-2303-11945.title: Unsupervised Cross-Domain Rumor Detection with Contrastive Learning and Cross-Attention
arxiv-2303-11945.creator: Hongyan Ran, Caiyan Jia
arxiv-2303-11945.description: Abstract Massive rumors usually appear along with breaking news or trending topics, seriously hindering the truth. Existing rumor detection methods are mostly focused on the same domain, thus have poor performance in cross-domain scenarios due to domain shift. In this work, we propose an end-to-end instance-wise and prototype-wise contrastive learning model with cross-attention mechanism for cross-domain rumor detection.

arxiv-2404-10964.title: Drawing Competitive Districts in Redistricting
arxiv-2404-10964.creator: Gabriel Chuang, Oussama Hanguir, Clifford Stein
arxiv-2404-10964.description: Abstract In the process of redistricting, one important metric is the number of competitive districts , that is, districts where both parties have a reasonable chance of winning a majority of votes. Competitive districts are important for achieving proportionality, responsiveness, and other desirable qualities; some states even directly list competitiveness in their legally-codified districting requirements.

arxiv-2405-06470.title: Solar fusion III: New data and theory for hydrogen-burning stars.
arxiv-2405-06470.creator: B. Acharya, M. Aliotta, A. B. Balantekin, D. Bemmerer, C. A. Bertulani, A. Best, C. R. Brune, R. Buompane, F. Cavanna, J. W. Chen, J. Colgan, A. Czarnecki, B. Davids, R. J. deBoer, F. Delahaye, R. Depalo, A. García, M. Gatu Johnson, D. Gazit, L. Gialanella, U. Greife, D. Guffanti, A. Guglielmetti, K
arxiv-2405-06470.description: Abstract In stars that lie on the main sequence in the Hertzsprung Russel diagram, like our Sun, hydrogen is fused to helium in a number of nuclear reaction chains and series, such as the proton-proton chain and the carbon-nitrogen-oxygen cycles. Precisely determined thermonuclear rates of these reactions lie at the foundation of the standard solar model.

arxiv-2501-08679.title: Diagonal Over-parameterization in Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces as an Adaptive Feature Model: Generalization and Adaptivity
arxiv-2501-08679.creator: Yicheng Li liyc22@mails.tsinghua.edu.cn, Qian Lin qianlin@tsinghua.edu.cn
arxiv-2501-08679.description: Abstract This paper introduces a diagonal adaptive kernel model that dynamically learns kernel eigenvalues and output coefficients simultaneously during training. Unlike fixed-kernel methods tied to the neural tangent kernel theory, the diagonal adaptive kernel model adapts to the structure of the truth function, significantly improving generalization over fixed-kernel methods, especially when the initial kernel is misaligned with the target.

arxiv-2507-10805.title: Impact of Cosmic Ray-driven Outflows on Lyman- α \alpha Emission in Cosmological Simulations
arxiv-2507-10805.creator: Taysun Kimm, Julien Devriendt, Francesco Rodríguez Montero, Adrianne Slyz, Jérémy Blaizot, Harley Katz, Beomchan Koh, Hyunmi Song
arxiv-2507-10805.description: Abstract Cosmic ray (CR) feedback has been proposed as a powerful mechanism for driving warm gas outflows in galaxies. We use cosmological magnetohydrodynamic simulations to investigate the impact of CR feedback on neutral hydrogen ( H I ) in a 10 11 ​ M ⊙ 10^{11}\,\mbox{$M_{\odot}$} dark matter halo at 2 < z < 4 2<z<4 .

arxiv-2510-02473.title: Two Proofs of the Hamiltonian Cycle Identity
arxiv-2510-02473.creator: Hamilton Sawczuk, Edinah Gnang
arxiv-2510-02473.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Hamilton Sawczuk, Edinah Gnang. The Hamiltonian cycle polynomial can be evaluated to count the number of Hamiltonian cycles in a graph. It can also be viewed as a list of all spanning cycles of length n n . We adopt the latter perspective and present a pair of original proofs for the Hamiltonian cycle identity which relates the Hamiltonian cycle polynomial to the important determinant and permanent polynomials. The first proof is a more accessible combinatorial argument.

arxiv-2601-03376.title: Weather-Aware Transformer for Real-Time Route Optimization in Drone-as-a-Service Operations
arxiv-2601-03376.creator: Kamal Mohamed 1 , Lillian Wassim 1 , Ali Hamdi 1 , Khaled Shaban 2
arxiv-2601-03376.description: Abstract This paper presents a novel framework to accelerate route prediction in Drone-as-a-Service operations through weather-aware deep learning models. While classical path-planning algorithms, such as A* and Dijkstra, provide optimal solutions, their computational complexity limits real-time applicability in dynamic environments. We address this limitation by training machine learning and deep learning models on synthetic datasets generated from classical algorithm simulations.

pmc-11477311.title: Leveraging Quality Improvement and Shared Learning to Improve Infant Well-Child Visit Rates in Texas
pmc-11477311.creator: Emily Stauffer Rocha, Susana Beatriz Peñate, Ryan D Van Ramshorst, Christopher R Cogle, Abdel-Latif Mohamed
pmc-11477311.description: Texas Medicaid improved infant well-child visit rates by participating in a national learning collaborative. The two-year program encouraged creativity and innovation in care for Medicaid recipients through partnerships with managed care organizations (MCOs). The MCO projects discovered valuable practices in member outreach and were disseminated in shared learning experiences.

pmc-11501524.title: Inverse design and optical vortex manipulation for thin-film absorption enhancement
pmc-11501524.creator: Munseong Bae, Jaegang Jo, Myunghoo Lee, Joonho Kang, Svetlana V. Boriskina, Haejun Chung
pmc-11501524.description: Optical vortices (OVs) have rapidly varying spatial phase and optical energy that circulates around points or lines of zero optical intensity. Manipulation of OVs offers innovative approaches for various fields, such as optical sensing, communication, and imaging. In this work, we demonstrate the correlation between OVs and absorption enhancement in two types of structures.

pmc-11596623.title: Differential Host Gene Expression in Response to Infection by Different Mycobacterium tuberculosis Strains—A Pilot Study
pmc-11596623.creator: Dewi Megawati, Lisa Y. Armitige, Loubna Tazi
pmc-11596623.description: Tuberculosis (TB) represents a global public health threat and is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Effective control of TB is complicated with the emergence of multidrug resistance. Yet, there is a fundamental gap in understanding the complex and dynamic interactions between different Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains and the host.

pmc-11640621.title: Role of Protein Tyrosine Phosphatases in Inflammatory Bowel Disease, Celiac Disease and Diabetes: Focus on the Intestinal Mucosa
pmc-11640621.creator: Claudia Bellomo, Francesca Furone, Roberta Rotondo, Ilaria Ciscognetti, Martina Carpinelli, Martina Nicoletti, Genoveffa D’Aniello, Leandra Sepe, Maria Vittoria Barone, Merlin Nanayakkara
pmc-11640621.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Protein tyrosine phosphatases (PTPs) are a family of enzymes essential for numerous cellular processes, such as cell growth, inflammation, differentiation, immune-mediated responses and oncogenic transformation. The aim of this review is to review the literature concerning the role of several PTPs—PTPN22, PTPN2, PTPN6, PTPN11, PTPσ, DUSP2, DUSP6 and PTPRK—at the level of the intestinal mucosa in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), celiac disease (CeD) and type 1 diabetes (T1D) in both in vitro and in vivo models.

pmc-11728475.title: A Mechanism of Reducing Methane Production During Sewage Sludge Composting by Adding Urea
pmc-11728475.creator: Ke Zhang, Haopeng Guo, Yujing Liang, Fuyong Liu, Guodi Zheng, Jun Zhang, Aihua Gao, Nan Liu, Chuang Ma
pmc-11728475.description: The study of the effect of the mechanism of urea addition to sewage sludge and sawdust-composting substrates on methane production is still limited. In the present study, the systematic investigation of the effect of urea addition (0.18, 0.9 and 1.8 kg) on methane production is discussed through the dynamics of physical properties, enzymes, and the microbial community during composting.

pmc-12644543.title: Geometric influence and multi-objective optimization of WEDM for hardened tool steels using ANN and NSGA-II
pmc-12644543.creator: Muhammad Sana, Muhammad Asad, Anamta Khan, Muhammad Umar Farooq, Sana Hassan, Saqib Anwar
pmc-12644543.description: Nowadays, due to their exceptional strength, hardness, and resistance to wear, hardened AISI D2 and DC53 tool steels are frequently used in the tool and die-making business. But these materials are difficult to machine conventionally because they include metallic carbides that are abrasive and shorten the life of the cutting tool.

pmc-12736567.title: Differential Balance Enhancements Associated with Conventional Balance Training and Portable Slackline Board Training: A Randomized Controlled Trial
pmc-12736567.creator: Trent Yamamoto, Joshua A. Kidwell, Vishruth Shatagopam, Kyle J. Hetherton, Eric V. Neufeld, Brett A. Dolezal
pmc-12736567.description: Compromised balance is implicated with increased injury risk in athletes. Although multiple modalities are available to improve balance, investigation into slackline balance training (SLT) has remained limited, especially in regard to elite athletes. The primary aim of this study was to determine the effects of SLT, using a novel portable slacklining board, on static and dynamic balance.

pmc-12748474.title: Confirming content validity of The Insomnia Daytime Symptoms and Impacts Questionnaire (IDSIQ) among adults with insomnia in four European countries
pmc-12748474.creator: Andrea Phillips-Beyer, Ariane K. Kawata, Leah Kleinman, Antonio Olivieri
pmc-12748474.description: BackgroundThe Insomnia Daytime Symptoms and Impacts Questionnaire (IDSIQ) v2.0 is a 14-item patient-reported outcome measure for assessing the daytime symptoms and impacts of insomnia. Content validity and measurement properties of the IDSIQ have been established among English-speakers. This study assessed content validity of translations of the IDSIQ, generated for use in clinical trials in non-English-speaking countries.

pmc-13056590.title: Association Between Statin Use and Non-Melanoma Skin Cancer Risk: A Distributed Network Analysis of 11 Real-World Databases
pmc-13056590.creator: Jiyoon An, Man S Kim, Yoonsung Lee, Bark-Lynn Lew, Soon-Hyo Kwon
pmc-13056590.description: BackgroundGiven the dual potential of statins to act as both carcinogenic and antineoplastic agents, evidence from previous investigations into statin use and the risk of nonmelanoma skin cancer (NMSC) remains inconclusive.ObjectiveTo demonstrate the impact of statin exposure on the NMSC risk in Korean patients.

pmc-13364983.title: Case Report: Interim success in treating pyogenic spondylitis caused by Staphylococcus epidermidis using UBE technology: a rare case
pmc-13364983.creator: Xiaxing Chen, Jianwei Rao
pmc-13364983.description: Background Pyogenic spondylitis is a spinal infection caused by non-specific pathogens, with pathological changes typically manifesting as purulent inflammation. The main causative agents include Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli, and others. In recent years, due to factors such as surgical procedures, diabetes mellitus, immunosuppression, and advanced age, the incidence of spinal infections has risen annually—posing significant challenges in diagnosis and treatment.

pmc-13453063.title: Acute Poisoning-Induced Rhabdomyolysis and Related Complications: A Report of Two Cases
pmc-13453063.creator: Manoranjan Behera, Akash Das, Dipti R Darjee, Rabindra Kisku, Aditya Pradhan
pmc-13453063.description: Rhabdomyolysis following acute poisoning is a rare complication. Acute poisoning with profenofos, an organophosphorus insecticide that irreversibly inhibits acetylcholinesterase, and Super Vasmol 33, a hair dye containing para-phenylenediamine, is associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Although rhabdomyolysis is an uncommon complication, it may precipitate acute kidney injury (AKI) and multiorgan dysfunction syndrome (MODS).

uslaw-usc-t10-s897.description: United States Code, Title 10 (Armed Forces); Part II (Personnel); Chapter 47 (Uniform Code Of Military Justice); Subchapter X (Punitive Articles).
